speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've had persistent bleeding after a wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; to start, have you noticed any bleeding from your gums or nose spontaneously, or only after minor injuries? Also, does this bleeding tend to last longer than usual or stop on its own quickly?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the family history of bleeding with joint swelling in your uncle suggests a potential factor VIII deficiency. Given your age and the specific history of hemarthrosis in your uncle, could you tell me if you have ever experienced joint pain or swelling in your knees or elbows after minor injuries? Also, have you noticed any prolonged bleeding from cuts on your arms or legs that took more than ten minutes to stop?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency). The clinical presentation of post-extraction bleeding, easy bruising, and a family history of hemarthrosis (joint swelling) in a male patient is classic for this condition.
